brief.headline: Samsung +11%, SK Hynix +8% on Iran ceasefire hopes—but gains eroded 50% intraday as Wall Street banks curb leverage
brief.summary: <cite index="39-1,40-15,40-16">Samsung surged over 12% and SK Hynix rose ~8-9% early June 12 on Trump's Iran ceasefire remarks, lifting KOSPI above 8%</cite>, but <cite index="45-1,45-2,45-11,45-12">gains retreated to under 8% and under 4% respectively after Wall Street banks including Morgan Stanley, Citi, and JPM tightened swap financing and rejected new leveraged bets on both names</cite>. <cite index="2-11,11-7,11-8">DRAM contract prices jumped 58-63% in Q2 following a record 90-95% Q1 surge, with NAND up 70-75% QoQ</cite>, while <cite index="2-15,2-24">HBM market is estimated at $54.6B in 2026 (+58% YoY), with SK Hynix projected to secure ~70% of HBM4 supply for Nvidia's Rubin</cite>. <cite index="22-5,22-9,26-8,26-9,26-10,26-11">The four hyperscalers will spend ~$700B capex in 2026 (Microsoft $190B, Amazon $200B, Alphabet $185B, Meta $125-145B), up 69% YoY</cite>, with <cite index="32-2,32-6">TSMC's CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S capacity fully booked by Nvidia, Google, Amazon, and MediaTek</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: <cite index="2-5,2-12,2-23,2-24">SK Hynix remains the clean HBM winner: industry expects it to anchor the supercycle with HBM3E leadership, world's first HBM4 mass production secured Sep 2025, and UBS projects ~70% HBM4 share for Nvidia Rubin in 2026</cite>. <cite index="44-8">Samsung is clawing back—customers say 'Samsung is back' on HBM4, but SK Hynix held 53% HBM share vs Samsung's 35% in Q3 2025</cite>. <cite index="6-2,6-3,6-9,6-10">Q1 2026 profits underscore the gap: Samsung semi OP was 53.7tr won ($36.1B, 94% of total), SK Hynix posted 52.6tr won revenue and 37.6tr won OP ($27.8B) on HBM strength</cite>. Near-term catalyst divergence: <cite index="45-15,45-16,45-22">both names account for ~50% of KOSPI, triggering ~$69B in passive selling since late October per GS; foreign outflows hit $70B YTD 2026 vs $20B in 2020 pandemic</cite>. Long SK Hynix vs short Samsung on HBM4 ramp timing and enterprise AI wallet share, but watch for Samsung 2nm foundry upside (Google I/O die talk circulating) and packaging expansion in Gwangju.

memory_cycle.stage: Mid-supercycle acceleration with structural tightness through 2027
memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="2-6,2-11">WSTS forecasts global semi market +25% YoY to $975B in 2026, memory segment +30%; BofA defines 2026 as supercycle akin to 1990s boom, predicting DRAM revenue +51%, NAND +45%, with ASPs up 33% and 26% respectively</cite>. <cite index="3-1">Goldman Sachs forecasts 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026 amid unprecedented demand and low inventory</cite>. <cite index="7-4,7-7,7-9">Producing 1 bit of HBM consumes ~3x the wafer capacity of DDR5; HBM margins incentivize capacity reallocation; AI will consume 20% of total DRAM production in 2026</cite>. <cite index="11-10,11-12,16-6,16-20">Cloud providers securing supply via long-term agreements; meaningful capacity expansion unlikely until late 2027, with TrendForce and Omdia expecting continued tightness into 2027</cite>. <cite index="1-14,6-13,6-20">Memory shortage driven by AI infra could persist until 2027 and beyond; supply never matching exploding demand despite massive capex</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="2-1,2-2,2-13,2-14">Global firms expect AI-specific memory demand centered on HBM to grow rapidly 2025-2028; some forecasts suggest HBM market size in 2028 will surpass entire DRAM market of 2024</cite>. <cite index="2-18,2-19">HBM3E remains 2026 flagship; Nvidia Blackwell Ultra, Google, and AWS are selecting HBM3E for proprietary ASIC-based AI chips</cite>. <cite index="2-16">Goldman forecasts HBM demand for custom ASIC chips will skyrocket 82% in 2026, accounting for 1/3 of market, indicating AI infra diversification beyond GPUs</cite>. <cite index="6-19,6-20,6-22">HBM manufacturing difficult and expensive, requiring advanced die stacking and packaging; supply limited, demand outpacing capacity build; manufacturers reallocating DRAM capacity toward high-margin HBM</cite>. <cite index="10-12,10-13">SK Hynix announced iHBM thermal packaging with integrated cooling elements, cutting thermal resistance >30% for high-temp, high-load environments</cite>. Watch: <cite index="9-4,9-5,9-6">Industry discussing separating GPUs and HBM into different packages connected via optical links, potentially allowing GPUs to support several times more HBM than current designs</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung +12%, SK Hynix +9% premarket on Trump Iran ceasefire, then cut in half by Wall Street swap curbs
news_pulse.implication: Geopolitical relief rally crushed by prime-broker risk limits. Morgan Stanley, Citi, JPM raised swap costs, rejected new levered bets on Samsung/SK Hynix/TSMC. Signals crowding in Korea semi single-names; $69B passive liquidation since Oct per GS. Intraday vol spike = derivative unwind risk.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers commit $700B capex in 2026, up 69% YoY; Morgan Stanley sees $740B global AI infra spend
news_pulse.implication: Microsoft $190B, Amazon $200B, Alphabet $185B, Meta $125-145B. Capex-to-revenue ratio rising from 10-15% to 25-30%. Sustained GPU/HBM/enterprise SSD demand through 2027. Memory pricing power intact; hyperscaler LTAs lock in allocation.

news_pulse.headline: Q2 2026 DRAM prices +58-63% QoQ, NAND +70-75%; Q1 saw record 90-95% DRAM jump, 55-60% NAND
news_pulse.implication: NAND now outpacing DRAM for first time this cycle. Enterprise SSD demand absorbing capacity; eMMC/UFS facing tightest supply. Suppliers reallocating to high-margin AI/server, disciplined on client. Memory ASP momentum sustains Samsung/SK Hynix margin expansion.

news_pulse.headline: BofA forecasts 2026 HBM market $54.6B (+58% YoY); Goldman sees HBM for custom ASICs +82%
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E dominant in 2026; HBM4 ramp starting with SK Hynix securing 70% of Nvidia Rubin supply per UBS. ASIC demand (Google TPU, AWS Trainium) diversifying HBM TAM beyond Nvidia. SK Hynix partnering with TSMC on packaging; Samsung playing catchup on qualification.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS-L and CoWoS-S fully booked; capacity scaling from 35k wpm late 2024 to 130k wpm by end 2026
news_pulse.implication: Nvidia securing >60% of total CoWoS capacity for 2025-26. Google, Amazon, MediaTek orders driving full utilization. AP8 and AP7 fabs ramping; CoPoS (panel-level) in development with supply-chain exclusivity. Advanced packaging remains bottleneck for AI accelerator shipments.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung Q1 2026 semi OP 53.7tr won ($36.1B, 94% of total profit); SK Hynix 37.6tr won OP on 52.6tr won revenue
news_pulse.implication: Record profitability on AI memory demand. Both expanding aggressively: SK Hynix M15X Cheongju (40k→80k wpm by 2027), Samsung P5 Pyeongtaek (2028 online). OpenAI Stargate deal: 900k DRAM wafers/month committed. Shortage extending to 2027.

news_pulse.headline: Goldman forecasts 4.9% DRAM supply deficit in 2026; memory shortages could last until 2027-28
news_pulse.implication: Structural undersupply driven by HBM capacity reallocation and slower fab ramp. Legacy DDR4/client DRAM facing tightest conditions. Pricing expected to remain elevated through 2028; new fabs take years to bring online.

news_pulse.headline: Leverage Shares lists 3x Samsung, 3x SK Hynix ETPs on LSE; Korean retail piles into double-leverage ETFs
news_pulse.implication: Global and local retail leverage amplifying volatility. 16 double-leverage ETFs launched in Korea in May with $2.8B day-1 AUM. Daily rebalancing creates gamma/vol feedback. Prime brokers now capping exposure—hedge fund swap rejection = unwind risk.

brief.derivatives_signal: <cite index="45-6,45-7">Major Wall Street banks (Citi, JPM, GS) increased financing costs for Samsung/SK Hynix/TSMC swaps, tightened new transaction scale, and rejected swap requests; Morgan Stanley no longer accepting new swaps for Samsung and SK Hynix, BofA, BNP, UBS also adjusting</cite>. <cite index="45-19,45-20">Korea launched 16 double-leveraged ETFs for Samsung/SK Hynix in late May with ~$2.8B assets on day 1; Goldman noted daily rebalancing could amplify volatility</cite>. <cite index="41-2,41-3,41-7,41-10">Leverage Shares listed 3x long Samsung (SMG3) and SK Hynix (HNX3) ETPs on LSE June 12, implemented via KRX futures with 3x exposure, channeling overseas demand into Korea derivatives</cite>. Net: dealer desks de-risking into retail leverage ramp = vol regime shift. Watch KRX futures basis, single-stock vol surfaces, and prime-broker margin calls if either name trades -5% intraday.
watch_for_next_3h: KOSPI intraday vol and Samsung/SK Hynix single-stock option skew if either tests -3% from session highs—signals forced unwind of levered retail/hedge positions
Any TSMC/Nvidia commentary on CoWoS allocation for H2 2026 or HBM4 qualification timing—impacts SK Hynix vs Samsung relative
